newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECHS AMBIVALENT ABOUT JOINING NATO - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: CZECHS AMBIVALENT ABOUT JOINING NATO - SURVEY.

text.p: Czechs are generally ambivalent to the idea of their country joining NATO, an opinion poll released on Wednesday showed.

The survey by the state-funded Institute for Public Opinion Research (IVVM) showed 38 percent support the country becoming one of the first former Soviet Bloc countries to join the western security alliance, while 35 percent oppose it.
A total of 27 percent of the scientific sample of 1,001 Czechs aged over 15 said they were undecided.
The Czechs, along with the Poles and the Hungarians, are widely seen as top candidates for NATO's planned expansion to former Warsaw Pact members.
Only 14 percent of Czechs in the survey said they were "definitely" in support of their country joining the group, while 18 percent said they were "definitely not" in favour.
In late October, U.S. President Bill Clinton called for the first former East Bloc members to join NATO by the year 2000.
The early November IVVM survey, taken after Clinton's much-publicised speech, showed Czech attitudes toward NATO basically unchanged from a similar survey a year ago.

The latest IVVM survey showed 33 percent see the main advantage of NATO membership as a guarantee of the country's security, while 40 percent regard the largest disadvantage coming in expected higher costs for the Czech army.
Czech politicians are still mixed on whether there should be a national referendum on NATO membership.

The centre-right ruling coalition parties -- the Civic Democratic Party of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, along with the junior Civic Democratic Aliance and Christian Democratic Union -- are all against a referendum on the issue.
The strongest opposition party, the Social Democrats support joining the alliance, but are insisting on a plebiscite to confirm the country's desire for membership.
Two other minor opposition parties, the Communists and the ultra-right Republicans are strongly against any plans for Czech membership in NATO.
